summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted following a report of a sensation of movement in his head, raising concern for possible CNS lymphoma progression. He has a history of composite Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with CNS relapse, previously treated with high-dose methotrexate. A non-contrast CT head showed no acute hemorrhage or mass effect. A subsequent MRI with contrast revealed no new enhancing lesions, hemorrhage, or edema, indicating stable disease. His symptoms were likely related to chronic brain changes from prior illness or treatment. He remained neurologically stable throughout admission, with no interventions required. He was discharged home with follow-up planned in neurology and oncology clinics.
